**Major clinical Effect of Rocuronium**:

- Non depolarising muscle relaxant
- Competitive antagonist at the nAChR at the NMJ
- Must block \~70% of all receptor sites before clinical effect seen, no way of measuring % receptor blockade by clinical measurement.   
- \>70% blockade progressive reduction in twitch height.
- ED95 Dose required to produce 95% reduction in twitch height in 50% of the population - for rocuronium this is 0.3mg/kg therefore ED95 Rocuronium =ED50 
- Typically the induction doses used are 2-5x the ED95. 

![](/content/exams/anzca/2013/B/13/standard-image3.jpeg){fig-alt="Rocuronium dose–response curve showing twitch depression and ED50 and ED95"}

**Factors encountered in clinical practice that may alter this curve:**

Factors potentiating NDMR BLOCK

Age: increased sensitising in neonates - due to immature  NMJ

Neuromuscular disorders i.e. myasthenia gravis

Drugs: inhaled anaesthetic, local anaesthetic

Electrolyte abnormalities: 

↑Mg ↑Na

↓K ↓Ca

Factors that ↑ resistance to NDMR

Anticholinesterase drug administration 

Presence of increased or extra junctional receptors: burns, prolonged immobilisation 

Motor neurone lesions 

Drugs that affect Rocuronium:

Potentate blockade:

- Local Anaesthetics
- Volatile agents
- Aminoglycosides
